text: We evaluated an auxiliary confidence loss on the strong student (aux_loss_weight 0.1) in a weak-to-strong setup where gpt2-small supervises mistral-7b, across num_seeds = 8 seeds. The weak supervisor reaches 0.62 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling accuracy is 0.81, while the strong student trained on weak labels attains a transfer accuracy of 0.63 (SE 0.02). The resulting performance gap recovered is 0.03 with a standard error of 0.13, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.12. The measured PGR therefore sits below the baseline, and in any case the standard error on PGR is far larger than the quantity itself, so these data do not support any claim that the auxiliary confidence loss helps; the result is compatible with no effect in either direction. The transfer accuracy estimate is much more tightly determined than the PGR, suggesting that the PGR noise stems largely from the narrow weak-to-strong accuracy range. Further seeds would be needed to resolve the direction of the effect.
